items.title: 'They got it all wrong': The miscalculation the US and Israel made over Iran
items.description: Donald Trump is deploying thousands of marines and extra battleships to the Middle East, while also claiming to be close to a deal with Iran to end the war. So is he set to wind down his war with Iran or is he thinking of escalating?

items.title: Trump under pressure to find an off-ramp amid oil and munitions crisis
items.description: While markets struggle to price a sudden collapse in oil supply military analysts are sounding the alarm on the rate countries are burning through weapons stockpiles.

items.title: Live: US-Israeli strikes hit two Iranian nuclear facilities
items.description: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio says America's war aims can be achieved without ground troops and operations will be complete in the "next couple of weeks". Follow live.

items.title: US 'on verge' of ending Iran war as Rubio demands allies lead postwar coalition
items.description: Secretary of State Marco Rubio tells G7 leaders to ready a postwar coalition to secure the Strait of Hormuz, saying the US-Israeli war on Iran could conclude within weeks.

items.title: Mapping Israel's destruction of Lebanese bridges
items.description: Israel's expanded invasion of southern Lebanon was at least 12 days in the making, with bridges targeted to effectively cut off the south from the country's centre.

items.title: This man went viral after surviving Bondi. Then the internet took a dark turn
items.description: Arsen Ostrovsky was on the ground, bleeding, at the Bondi attack when he decided to take a selfie. Within 2 hours it was circulating on the internet. In less than a day, it had become fodder for a global conspiracy theory.

items.title: For Australia, the end of the Iran war might just be the start
items.description: The federal government is turning its mind to what Australian support in the Middle East might look like after a ceasefire.

items.title: Tiger Woods arrested following car crash near Florida home
items.description: Golf legend Tiger Woods is arrested in Florida after refusing to submit a urine sample following a car crash near his Florida home.

items.title: Live: Ex-Cyclone Narelle downgraded as it continues to track along West coast
items.description: The storm, which has already made landfall in Far North Queensland and the Northern Territory, is now impacting the WA coast.

items.title: Dementia is Australia's top killer, yet most still miss the early signs
items.description: Dementia is the leading cause of death in Australia and stigmas around the disease can delay diagnosis. But some in the community are at work to break taboos.

items.title: 'Built on deception': How one online travel site is fleecing customers
items.description: As holiday-makers gear up for Easter, online travel site Guest Reservations is accused of fleecing customers using hidden fees and charges with advocates calling on government and the regulator to step in.

items.title: Do we actually have the workforce for the $4b NDIS alternative?
items.description: Months away from the start of a huge shift in disability support for children, the workforce expected to deliver it has concerns about its readiness.

items.title: Ranked number one on the terrorism index, this nation struck back
items.description: As global attention remains fixed on the sprawling war in the Middle East, another conflict is edging towards a dangerous threshold — one between nuclear-armed Pakistan and Taliban-controlled Afghanistan.

items.title: Head of TGA speaks out on sunscreen scandal
items.description: In his first interview since the sunscreen controversy erupted almost 10 months ago, the Therapeutic Goods Administration head says he hopes the proposed shake-up of regulations will restore consumer confidence.

items.title: As music festivals collapse, one scrappy underdog is making a lot of noise
items.description: As music festivals collapse, one Geelong kid's hobby has turned into a big day out.

items.title: The nine books that knocked our critics' socks off this month
items.description: Wondering what to read next? Gothic crime fiction, a cult Japanese bestseller and a fantastical twist on the Blitz are among our critics' latest recommendations.

items.title: Our critics can't stop listening to these 10 albums from March
items.description: The year might've kicked off with a flood of great records, but March is when things really snap into gear.

items.title: Is government intervention keeping LNG exporters on their 'best behaviour'?
items.description: With war in the Middle East throwing energy markets into chaos, Australian gas prices are strikingly subdued. Experts say looming intervention by Canberra may explain why.

items.title: 'It's about fairness': Australian Iranians hit back at 'racist' visa ban
items.description: Thousands of Iranian travellers have been barred from entering Australia under a government ban targeting people who might overstay their visas, prompting criticism by refugee advocates.

items.title: Iran's soccer team honours victims of deadly airstrike on primary school
items.description: Iran soccer players hold small backpacks to honour the victims of a deadly missile strike on a girls' primary school, before a friendly against Nigeria.

items.title: 'Stay in your lane': Experts urge against following running influencer advice
items.description: Recently, online discussion has turned to what some perceive to be a spate of influencers getting injured.

items.title: A century ago, a Liberal Party disintegrated, and there are lessons for its namesake
items.description: Last week's South Australian election has left the Liberals in the grip of what one analyst described as an "existential crisis". As the Liberals seek to learn the lessons of the past, they should bear in mind the example of their once mighty namesakes, who ruled Britain for decades before their party turned to dust.

items.title: Savannah Guthrie to return to Today show after mother's disappearance
items.description: Savannah Guthrie is scheduled to return to her job as a co-anchor of NBC's Today show on April 6, more than two months after her 84-year-old mother's unresolved abduction.

items.title: End of an era for general store owned by family for 100 years
items.description: The Tharwa General Store — which has been run by the same family since 1926 — has been many things: a post office, a mechanic's workshop, a fuel stop, a lolly shop, a watering hole, and above all, a place where a community comes together.

items.title: Blueberry industry under scrutiny amid rapid growth
items.description: Australians are eating and growing more blueberries than ever before, but questions are being asked about how production of the fruit is being regulated.
